role_and_message.evidence: The full AccessWorld F task/setup, OpenClaw interaction and grader overview remains the original figure with a single result-label addition.

panel_and_object_coverage.evidence: Task JSON, Guest worker, agent, a11y-tools, four AT conditions, application icons and all four example cards remain unchanged outside the added label.

labels_math_and_numbers.evidence: The source task wording, key combinations, click coordinates, Voice Control phrases and Team lunch check are preserved pixel-for-pixel.

connections_and_direction.evidence: Setup and grade directions, action/observation pair, commands/output pair and AT/app feedback arrows retain exactly their original pixels.

visual_encodings.evidence: Original gray, blue, green and orange AT encodings and all icons remain unchanged.

examples_and_data.evidence: Four AT example cards match source pixels exactly; additionally a full-image difference check confines every changed pixel to the Grading result text patch.

unsupported_additions.evidence: Section 3.1 describes a grader inspecting the resulting computer state and producing a binary score; Grading result labels the existing checked return.

complete_visible_content.evidence: The single new label is above the return arrow without covering Team lunch, endpoints, examples or another label.

remaining_limitations: Source resolution and retained source ambiguities remain. Quality is evaluated separately without source metadata.
caption:
Figure 1: AccessWorld Overview. Each task has an instruction and grader, with task-specific
setup when needed, and runs in the same macOS virtual machine. OpenClaw connects the agent to
standard computer use, VoiceOver, Voice Control, or Zoom. The task and grader stay fixed while
the available observations and actions change with the interaction condition.
